records.k: fader slider number index 推桿 滑桿 編號
records.d: Returns the position of fader number n, from 0 to 1: the same as fader1 to fader8, for any n.
records.x: The function form of fader1, for when the fader's number is a variable. n Which fader, counting from 1. The fader's position, 0..1; 0 until it has moved.

records.k: fader slider number index 推桿 滑桿 編號
records.d: 回傳第 n 支推桿的位置，0 到 1：跟 fader1 到 fader8 一樣，但 n 可以是任何數字。
records.x: fader1 的函式版本，推桿的編號是變數的時候用。 n 第幾支推桿，從 1 開始算。 推桿的位置，0..1。還沒推過之前是 0。

records.a: fader1 fader2 fader3 fader4 fader5 fader6 fader7 fader8
records.k: fader slider controller midi 推桿 滑桿 控制器 midi
records.d: The position of a controller fader (slider), from 0 to 1: fader1 is the first fader, up to fader8.
records.x: Works exactly like knob1, for the controller's faders, numbered in the order the controller's profile lists them (as printed on the device). A controller with only four faders, like the MiniLab 3, has fader1 to fader4. Nothing to call; reading a fader asks for Web MIDI, like a knob. Changes when the fader moves; 0 until it has moved.

records.a: fader1 fader2 fader3 fader4 fader5 fader6 fader7 fader8
records.k: fader slider controller midi 推桿 滑桿 控制器 midi
records.d: 控制器上推桿（滑桿）的位置，從 0 到 1：fader1 是第一支推桿，一直到 fader8。
records.x: 用法跟 knob1 完全一樣，只是對應控制器上的推桿，編號依控制器設定檔列出的順序（也就是機器上印的順序）。只有四支推桿的控制器（像 MiniLab 3）就只有 fader1 到 fader4。 不用呼叫任何東西。讀推桿就會像旋鈕一樣去要 Web MIDI。 推桿移動的時候才會改變。還沒推過之前是 0。

records.k: fader moved slider callback event 推桿 滑桿 事件 回呼
records.d: You define this function; oav-p5 calls it whenever a fader moves.
records.x: The fader twin of knobMoved(): function faderMoved(n, value) { … }. n Which fader (1 is the first). value Where it is now, 0..1.

records.k: fader moved slider callback event 推桿 滑桿 事件 回呼
records.d: 你來定義這個函式。推桿一移動，oav-p5 就呼叫它。
records.x: knobMoved() 的推桿版本：function faderMoved(n, value) { … }。 n 哪一支推桿（1 是第一支）。 value 現在的位置，0..1。

records.k: knob dial number index controller 旋鈕 編號 控制器
records.d: Returns the position of knob number n, from 0 to 1: the same as knob1 to knob8, for any n.
records.x: Use it when the number of the knob is a variable: for (let i = 1; i <= 16; i++) bar(i, knob(i));. It also works in a sketch that has its own knob1, which oav-p5 then leaves alone. n Which knob, counting from 1 (as printed on the controller). The knob's position, 0..1; 0 until it has been turned.

records.k: knob dial number index controller 旋鈕 編號 控制器
records.d: 回傳第 n 顆旋鈕的位置，0 到 1：跟 knob1 到 knob8 一樣，但 n 可以是任何數字。
records.x: 旋鈕的編號是變數的時候用它：for (let i = 1; i <= 16; i++) bar(i, knob(i));。草圖自己已經有 knob1 的話也可以用，oav-p5 不會去動那個名稱。 n 第幾顆旋鈕，從 1 開始算（照控制器上印的）。 旋鈕的位置，0..1。還沒轉過之前是 0。

records.a: knob1 knob2 knob3 knob4 knob5 knob6 knob7 knob8
records.k: knob dial rotary controller cc control change midi potentiometer 旋鈕 控制器 轉鈕 midi 控制訊號
records.d: The position of a controller knob, from 0 to 1: knob1 is the first knob, knob2 the second, up to knob8.
records.x: Read it in draw() the way you read mouseX: background(knob1 255). Knobs are numbered the way they are printed on the controller, so knob 1 is knob 1 on any controller OAV has a profile for: the MiniLab 3's first knob is CC 74, the LPD8's is CC 70. The sketch never needs to know a CC number. On a controller OAV has no profile for, the first knob you turn becomes knob1, the next one knob2, and so on, in the order you turn them. Past eight, use knob(n). Nothing to call. Reading a knob tells oav-p5 the sketch plays from MIDI, so it asks the browser for Web MIDI (Chrome, Edge, Firefox; Safari and iPad have none: use 🎹 or a phone there). A sketch that already has its own knob1 (a let, a function) keeps it, and a card beside the 🎹 says what to read instead (knob(1)). With OP Configurator, knobs also drive the OPC sliders in the order they are declared. A knob the sketch reads itself stays the sketch's: that slider no longer follows it. Changes when the knob moves, not once per frame; the sketch just reads the latest value. 0 until the knob has been turned.

records.a: knob1 knob2 knob3 knob4 knob5 knob6 knob7 knob8
records.k: knob dial rotary controller cc control change midi potentiometer 旋鈕 控制器 轉鈕 midi 控制訊號
records.d: 控制器上旋鈕的位置，從 0 到 1：knob1 是第一顆旋鈕，knob2 是第二顆，一直到 knob8。
records.x: 像讀 mouseX 一樣在 draw() 裡讀：background(knob1 255)。旋鈕的編號照控制器上印的順序，所以在 OAV 有設定檔的任何控制器上，旋鈕 1 就是旋鈕 1：MiniLab 3 的第一顆是 CC 74，LPD8 的是 CC 70。草圖完全不用知道 CC 號碼。 遇到 OAV 沒有設定檔的控制器，你轉的第一顆旋鈕就變成 knob1，下一顆是 knob2，依你轉的順序往下排。超過八顆就用 knob(n)。 不用呼叫任何東西。讀旋鈕就等於告訴 oav-p5 這份草圖要用 MIDI 玩，它會向瀏覽器要 Web MIDI（Chrome、Edge、Firefox 有。Safari 和 iPad 沒有，那裡改用 🎹 或手機）。 草圖如果本來就有自己的 knob1（let、函式都算），就由草圖保留，🎹 旁邊會有一張卡片說明改讀什麼（knob(1)）。 搭配 OP Configurator 時，旋鈕也會依宣告順序推動 OPC 的滑桿。草圖自己有讀的那顆旋鈕就歸草圖：對應的滑桿不再跟著動。 旋鈕轉動的時候才會改變，不是每個畫面一次。草圖只要讀最新的值。旋鈕還沒轉過之前是 0。

records.k: knob moved callback event turn 旋鈕 轉動 事件 回呼
records.d: You define this function; oav-p5 calls it whenever a knob moves.
records.x: Like mouseMoved() for knobs: It is called for every step the knob sends, so many times per second while it turns. To read a knob once a frame, use knob1 instead. n Which knob (1 is the first, as printed on the controller). value Where it is now, 0..1.

records.k: knob moved callback event turn 旋鈕 轉動 事件 回呼
records.d: 你來定義這個函式。旋鈕一轉動，oav-p5 就呼叫它。
records.x: 就像旋鈕版的 mouseMoved()： 旋鈕每送出一格就呼叫一次，轉動的時候每秒會呼叫很多次。想要每個畫面讀一次，就改用 knob1。 n 哪一顆旋鈕（1 是第一顆，照控制器上印的）。 value 現在的位置，0..1。

records.k: note key pitch keyboard midi number 音符 琴鍵 音高 鍵盤 midi 號碼
records.d: The MIDI number (0 to 127) of the last key pressed.
records.x: Middle C is 60, A4 is 69. noteName(note) writes the number as a name (60 → 'C4') and noteFreq(note) as a frequency in Hz. velocity says how hard it was pressed. For every key, not just the last, define notePressed(). Unlike knob1, reading it does not by itself ask for Web MIDI: a sketch that defines notePressed() or reads a knob or pad does. 🎹 and a phone always work. A sketch with its own note (a let note, a function) keeps it; read midi.last.note instead. oav-p5 says so in a card the first time. Set when a key goes down and kept after it is released; 0 before any key has been pressed.

records.k: note key pitch keyboard midi number 音符 琴鍵 音高 鍵盤 midi 號碼
records.d: 最後被按下的那個鍵的 MIDI 號碼（0 到 127）。
records.x: 中央 C 是 60，A4 是 69。noteName(note) 把號碼寫成音名（60 → 'C4'），noteFreq(note) 換成赫茲。velocity 告訴你按得多用力。想要每個鍵都知道、不只最後一個，就定義 notePressed()。 跟 knob1 不一樣，單單讀它不會去要 Web MIDI：草圖有定義 notePressed()，或讀了旋鈕、墊子，才會去要。🎹 和手機隨時都能用。 草圖如果自己有 note（let note、函式都算），就由草圖保留。改讀 midi.last.note。oav-p5 第一次會用卡片告訴你。 鍵按下的時候設定，放開之後也保留。還沒有按過任何鍵之前是 0。

records.k: key down held keyIsDown note name C4 按著 琴鍵 音名 keyIsDown
records.d: True while the key n (a MIDI number or a name like 'C4') is held down.
records.x: The MIDI version of keyIsDown(). noteIsDown('C4') is the same as noteIsDown(60): C4 is middle C. A name that is not a note ('H4', 'C-2') stops the sketch with a one-line card saying how to write it. n The key: a MIDI number (60) or a note name ('C4', 'c#4', 'Db3'). True if that key is down right now.

records.k: key down held keyIsDown note name C4 按著 琴鍵 音名 keyIsDown
records.d: 鍵 n（MIDI 號碼，或像 'C4' 這樣的音名）按著的時候是 true。
records.x: 就是 MIDI 版的 keyIsDown()。noteIsDown('C4') 跟 noteIsDown(60) 一樣：C4 是中央 C。不是音符的名稱（'H4'、'C-2'）會讓草圖停下來，並用一張卡片告訴你怎麼寫。 n 哪個鍵：MIDI 號碼（60）或音名（'C4'、'c#4'、'Db3'）。 那個鍵現在按著就是 true。

records.k: key pressed held any key keyIsPressed 按著 任一個鍵 琴鍵
records.d: True while at least one key is held down.
records.x: To ask about one particular key, use noteIsDown(). midi.held lists every key held right now, lowest first. Like keyIsPressed, for MIDI keys. False when nothing is held.

records.k: key pressed held any key keyIsPressed 按著 任一個鍵 琴鍵
records.d: 只要有任何一個鍵按著，就是 true。
records.x: 想問某一個特定的鍵，用 noteIsDown()。midi.held 列出現在按著的所有鍵，由低到高。 像 keyIsPressed，但是對 MIDI 琴鍵。沒有任何鍵按著就是 false。

records.k: key pressed note on callback event keyboard 按下 琴鍵 事件 回呼 鍵盤
records.d: You define this function; oav-p5 calls it each time a key (or a pad) goes down.
records.x: Declare it the way you declare keyPressed(): It is called once per key, with the key and how hard. A pad also calls it, unless the sketch defines padPressed(). Defining it is enough: oav-p5 sees the function and asks for Web MIDI. Keys from 🎹 and from a phone call it too. An error inside it does not stop the music: the next key still plays, and the message shows in the console and on a card beside the 🎹, with the file and line. note The MIDI number of the key (60 is middle C). noteName(note) turns it into a name. velocity How hard, 0..1.

records.k: key pressed note on callback event keyboard 按下 琴鍵 事件 回呼 鍵盤
records.d: 你來定義這個函式。每當有一個鍵（或打擊墊）按下，oav-p5 就呼叫它。
records.x: 用宣告 keyPressed() 的方式宣告它： 每個鍵呼叫一次，帶著是哪個鍵、多用力。打擊墊也會呼叫它，除非草圖有定義 padPressed()。 只要定義了它就夠了：oav-p5 看到這個函式，就會去要 Web MIDI。🎹 和手機上彈的鍵也會呼叫它。 裡面出錯不會讓音樂停掉：下一個鍵還是照樣處理，錯誤訊息會出現在 console，也會在 🎹 旁邊的卡片上顯示檔案與行號。 note 這個鍵的 MIDI 號碼（60 是中央 C）。noteName(note) 可以把它轉成音名。 velocity 多用力，0..1。

records.k: key released note off callback event 放開 琴鍵 事件 回呼
records.d: You define this function; oav-p5 calls it each time a key (or a pad) is let go.
records.x: The partner of notePressed(), like keyReleased() to keyPressed(): note The MIDI number of the key that was released.

records.k: key released note off callback event 放開 琴鍵 事件 回呼
records.d: 你來定義這個函式。每當有一個鍵（或打擊墊）放開，oav-p5 就呼叫它。
records.x: notePressed() 的另一半，就像 keyReleased() 之於 keyPressed()： note 被放開的那個鍵的 MIDI 號碼。

records.k: pad drum pad index velocity 打擊墊 墊子 編號 力道
records.d: Returns how hard pad number n is pressed, 0 to 1: the same as pad1 to pad16, for any n.
records.x: The function form of pad1. n Which pad, counting from 1. The velocity while the pad is held (0..1), 0 when it is released.

records.k: pad drum pad index velocity 打擊墊 墊子 編號 力道
records.d: 回傳第 n 個打擊墊被按得多用力，0 到 1：跟 pad1 到 pad16 一樣，但 n 可以是任何數字。
records.x: pad1 的函式版本。 n 第幾個墊子，從 1 開始算。 墊子按著的時候是力道（0..1），放開是 0。

records.a: pad1 pad2 pad3 pad4 pad5 pad6 pad7 pad8 pad9 pad10 pad11 pad12 pad13 pad14 pad15 pad16
records.k: pad drum pad button velocity trigger controller 打擊墊 墊子 按鍵 力道 觸發 控制器
records.d: How hard a drum pad is pressed, from 0 to 1: pad1 is the first pad, up to pad16; 0 when it is let go.
records.x: Read it like a held mouse button that also knows how hard: if (pad1 > 0) fill(255, 90, 31). Pads are numbered in the order the controller's profile lists them. To react once per hit rather than ask every frame, define padPressed(). Nothing to call; reading a pad asks for Web MIDI, like a knob. The velocity of the hit while the pad is held (1 is as hard as the controller sends), and 0 as soon as it is released.

records.a: pad1 pad2 pad3 pad4 pad5 pad6 pad7 pad8 pad9 pad10 pad11 pad12 pad13 pad14 pad15 pad16
records.k: pad drum pad button velocity trigger controller 打擊墊 墊子 按鍵 力道 觸發 控制器
records.d: 打擊墊被按得多用力，從 0 到 1：pad1 是第一個墊子，一直到 pad16。放開就是 0。
records.x: 像一個知道力道的滑鼠按鍵那樣讀：if (pad1 > 0) fill(255, 90, 31)。墊子編號依控制器設定檔列出的順序。想「每打一下反應一次」而不是每個畫面都問，就定義 padPressed()。 不用呼叫任何東西。讀墊子就會像旋鈕一樣去要 Web MIDI。 墊子按著的時候是這一下的力道（1 是控制器能送出的最大力道），一放開就變成 0。

records.k: pad hit drum pad callback event trigger 打擊墊 事件 回呼 觸發
records.d: You define this function; oav-p5 calls it each time a drum pad is hit.
records.x: When the sketch defines padPressed(), a pad calls it and not notePressed(); without it, a pad calls notePressed() like any key. n Which pad (1 is the first). velocity How hard, 0..1.

records.k: pad hit drum pad callback event trigger 打擊墊 事件 回呼 觸發
records.d: 你來定義這個函式。每打一下打擊墊，oav-p5 就呼叫它一次。
records.x: 草圖有定義 padPressed() 的話，打擊墊會呼叫它，而不會呼叫 notePressed()。沒有定義的話，打擊墊會像任何一個鍵一樣呼叫 notePressed()。 n 哪個墊子（1 是第一個）。 velocity 多用力，0..1。

records.k: pad released callback event 打擊墊 放開 事件 回呼
records.d: You define this function; oav-p5 calls it each time a drum pad is let go.
records.x: The partner of padPressed(): function padReleased(n) { … }. Without it, a pad calls noteReleased(). n Which pad (1 is the first).

records.k: pad released callback event 打擊墊 放開 事件 回呼
records.d: 你來定義這個函式。每當打擊墊放開，oav-p5 就呼叫它。
records.x: padPressed() 的另一半：function padReleased(n) { … }。沒有定義的話，打擊墊會呼叫 noteReleased()。 n 哪個墊子（1 是第一個）。

records.k: velocity force how hard dynamics 力道 力度 多用力 強弱
records.d: How hard the last key was pressed, from 0 to 1.
records.x: MIDI sends velocity as 0 to 127; oav-p5 hands you it divided by 127, so 1 is the hardest hit the controller can send. A sketch with its own velocity keeps it; read midi.last.value. Set together with note when a key goes down; kept after release; 0 before any key.

records.k: velocity force how hard dynamics 力道 力度 多用力 強弱
records.d: 最後那個鍵被按得多用力，從 0 到 1。
records.x: MIDI 的力道是 0 到 127。oav-p5 給你的是除以 127 之後的值，所以 1 就是控制器能送出的最大力道。 草圖自己有 velocity 的話就由草圖保留。改讀 midi.last.value。 跟 note 一起在鍵按下的時候設定。放開之後保留。還沒按過任何鍵之前是 0。

records.k: play send note trigger simulate virtual key 彈 送出音符 觸發 模擬 虛擬琴鍵
records.d: Plays a key as if a controller did: midi.play(60, 0.8) presses middle C, midi.play(60, 0) lets it go.
records.x: It sends the same MIDI bytes a keyboard would, with midi.last.source set to 'screen', so everything reacts: notePressed(), noteIsDown(), note, the sound if startSound() is on. midi and OAVp5 are the same object, so OAVp5.play and midi.play are one function. The key stays down until you play it again with velocity 0. note The key: a MIDI number or a name ('C#4'). velocity How hard, 0..1; 0 releases the key. Leave it out for full force.

records.k: play send note trigger simulate virtual key 彈 送出音符 觸發 模擬 虛擬琴鍵
records.d: 像控制器那樣彈一個鍵：midi.play(60, 0.8) 按下中央 C，midi.play(60, 0) 放開。
records.x: 它送出的 MIDI 位元組跟鍵盤送出的一樣，midi.last.source 會是 'screen'，所以所有東西都會有反應：notePressed()、noteIsDown()、note，還有開著 startSound() 時的聲音。midi 和 OAVp5 是同一個物件，所以 OAVp5.play 和 midi.play 是同一個函式。 鍵會一直按著，直到你再用力道 0 彈一次。 note 哪個鍵：MIDI 號碼或音名（'C#4'）。 velocity 多用力，0..1。0 表示放開。不給就是最大力道。

records.k: frequency hz pitch tuning A440 oscillator 頻率 赫茲 音高 調音 振盪器
records.d: Returns the frequency in Hz of a note: noteFreq('A4') is 440.
records.x: For a sketch that makes its own sound (p5.sound, Web Audio): osc.freq(noteFreq(note)). If you just want the sound, startSound() plays every key for you. v A note name or a MIDI number. A number may be fractional (69.5 is a quarter tone above A4) and is not held to 0..127. Hz, equal temperament with A4 = 69 = 440 Hz.

records.k: frequency hz pitch tuning A440 oscillator 頻率 赫茲 音高 調音 振盪器
records.d: 回傳音符的頻率（赫茲）：noteFreq('A4') 是 440。
records.x: 給自己發聲的草圖用（p5.sound、Web Audio）：osc.freq(noteFreq(note))。如果只是想要有聲音，startSound() 會幫你把每個鍵都彈出來。 v 音名或 MIDI 號碼。數字可以有小數（69.5 是比 A4 高四分之一音），而且不會被限制在 0..127。 赫茲，十二平均律，A4 = 69 = 440 Hz。

records.k: note name midi number C4 convert sharp flat display 音名 midi 號碼 轉換 升記號 降記號
records.d: Turns a MIDI number into a note name: noteName(61) is 'C#4'.
records.x: notePressed(note, velocity) hands you the number; noteName(note) writes it back as a name for the screen or a lookup table. The same C4-is-60 convention as noteNumber(). v A MIDI number (or a name, which is normalised). o Options: { flats: true } writes 'Db4' instead of 'C#4'; { octave: false } drops the octave number ('C#'). The name, sharps by default: noteName(60) is 'C4'.

records.k: note name midi number C4 convert sharp flat display 音名 midi 號碼 轉換 升記號 降記號
records.d: 把 MIDI 號碼轉成音名：noteName(61) 是 'C#4'。
records.x: notePressed(note, velocity) 給你的是號碼。noteName(note) 把它寫回音名，拿去顯示在畫面上或查表。跟 noteNumber() 一樣，C4 就是 60。 v MIDI 號碼（給音名的話會被整理成標準寫法）。 o 選項：{ flats: true } 寫成 'Db4' 而不是 'C#4'。{ octave: false } 不寫八度數字（'C#'）。 音名，預設用升記號：noteName(60) 是 'C4'。

records.k: note name midi number C4 convert pitch sharp flat 音名 midi 號碼 轉換 音高 升記號 降記號
records.d: Turns a note name like 'C4' into its MIDI number, 0 to 127.
records.x: A name is a letter A to G (either case), an optional # or b (♯ and ♭ too), and the octave: C4, c#4, Db3, C-1 (0) up to G9 (127). C4 is 60. Anything else, such as 'H4' or 'C-2', throws an error, and a card beside the 🎹 says how to write a note. You rarely call it yourself: every place that takes a note number also takes a name, such as noteIsDown() and midi.play(). v A note name ('C4', 'c#4', 'Db3', 'F♯2') or a number. A number comes back rounded and held to 0..127. The MIDI number: noteNumber('C4') is 60, noteNumber('A4') is 69.

records.k: note name midi number C4 convert pitch sharp flat 音名 midi 號碼 轉換 音高 升記號 降記號
records.d: 把像 'C4' 這樣的音名轉成 MIDI 號碼，0 到 127。
records.x: 音名由一個 A 到 G 的字母（大小寫都可以）、可有可無的 # 或 b（♯、♭ 也行），加上八度數字組成：C4、c#4、Db3，從 C-1（0）到 G9（127）。C4 是 60。 其他寫法（像 'H4'、'C-2'）會丟出錯誤，🎹 旁邊也會有一張卡片告訴你音名怎麼寫。 通常不用自己呼叫：凡是收音符號碼的地方也都收音名，像 noteIsDown() 和 midi.play()。 v 音名（'C4'、'c#4'、'Db3'、'F♯2'）或數字。數字會四捨五入並限制在 0..127。 MIDI 號碼：noteNumber('C4') 是 60，noteNumber('A4') 是 69。

records.k: bass mid treble low high frequency band spectrum equalizer fft 低音 中音 高音 頻段 頻率 頻譜 麥克風
records.d: How much of the microphone's sound is low (bass), middle (mid) or high (treble), each from 0 to 1.
records.x: Use them like micLevel, one number per band: fill(200 + bass 160, 70, 100) pushes the colour with the low end. The three share one entry because they behave the same; only the frequency range differs. Unlike micLevel they are not measured in decibels: each is the average strength of the frequencies in its band, scaled by micSensitivity() and held to 1. A band that is faint in your room can stay close to 0; raise the sensitivity rather than multiplying by a large number. Reading any of them asks for the microphone the first time, exactly like micLevel; until you allow it they are 0. A sketch that already has its own variable, function or library called bass, mid or treble keeps it: oav-p5 leaves that name alone and never starts the microphone for it. Assigning one later turns the name back into a plain variable. The energy in 20–250 Hz (bass), 250–2000 Hz (mid) and 2000–8000 Hz (treble). Updated once per display frame while the microphone is on; 0 otherwise.

records.k: bass mid treble low high frequency band spectrum equalizer fft 低音 中音 高音 頻段 頻率 頻譜 麥克風
records.d: 麥克風聽到的聲音裡，低音（bass）、中音（mid）、高音（treble）各佔多少，各自從 0 到 1。
records.x: 用法跟 micLevel 一樣，每個頻段一個數字：fill(200 + bass 160, 70, 100) 讓顏色跟著低音走。三個名稱共用這一條，因為它們的行為完全相同，只有頻率範圍不同。 跟 micLevel 不一樣，它們不是用分貝量的：每一個是該頻段所有頻率的平均強度，乘上 micSensitivity() 之後最多算到 1。如果某個頻段在你的房間裡很微弱，數字會一直貼近 0。這時調高靈敏度，比自己乘一個很大的數字好。 第一次讀其中任何一個，就會跟 micLevel 一樣去要麥克風。在你允許之前都是 0。 如果草圖本來就有自己的 bass、mid 或 treble（變數、函式、函式庫都算），oav-p5 就不動那個名稱，也不會為它去開麥克風。之後自己指定值的話，那個名稱就變回一般變數。 bass 是 20–250 Hz 的能量，mid 是 250–2000 Hz，treble 是 2000–8000 Hz。麥克風開著時每個畫面更新一次，其他時候是 0。

records.k: beat onset tempo rhythm clap trigger transient 拍子 節拍 節奏 鼓點 觸發 麥克風
records.d: True for one frame each time the microphone (or the drum machine) hears a beat.
records.x: It behaves like mouseIsPressed while a button is down, except the "press" lasts one frame: if (beat) flash = 1; is all it takes to react to the music. A beat is a jump in loudness over what the room has been doing, with at least 100 ms between two beats; two beats between two frames count as one. When the drum machine is playing, beat is also true for a frame on every kick and snare, so a sketch written for the microphone moves over to the machine unchanged. Reading beat asks for the microphone the first time, like micLevel. If you would rather be called, define beatDetected(). True in the first draw() after a beat, and false until the next one. Reading it twice in the same frame gives the same answer.

records.k: beat onset tempo rhythm clap trigger transient 拍子 節拍 節奏 鼓點 觸發 麥克風
records.d: 麥克風（或鼓機）每聽到一個拍子，就在那一個畫面是 true。
records.x: 它的用法像按著滑鼠鍵時的 mouseIsPressed，只是「按下」只持續一個畫面：if (beat) flash = 1; 就能對音樂做出反應。一個拍子是音量比房間一直以來的聲音突然跳高，兩個拍子之間至少隔 100 毫秒。兩個畫面之間發生的兩個拍子只算一次。 鼓機在播的時候，每一下大鼓和小鼓也會讓 beat 在那個畫面是 true，所以為麥克風寫的草圖不用改就能換成鼓機。 第一次讀 beat 就會跟 micLevel 一樣去要麥克風。如果你比較想被呼叫，就定義 beatDetected()。 拍子之後的第一個 draw() 是 true，到下一個拍子之前都是 false。同一個畫面裡讀兩次，答案一樣。

records.k: beat callback event onset rhythm clap 拍子 事件 回呼 節拍 節奏 麥克風
records.d: You define this function; oav-p5 calls it each time the microphone (or the drum machine) hears a beat.
records.x: Declare it the way you declare keyPressed(): It is called once per beat, right when the beat lands, not once per frame. Use beat instead if you would rather ask each frame. A sketch that defines beatDetected() and reads no microphone value starts the microphone on the first click or key. When the drum machine is on, the same function is called for its kicks and snares and the microphone is not opened for it. OAVp5.mic.on('beat', fn) is the same thing without defining a global; it returns a function that stops listening. If your function throws, the sketch keeps running: the error appears in the console and as a card beside the 🎹 with the file and line. level How loud it was at that moment, 0..1 (the value of micLevel).

records.k: beat callback event onset rhythm clap 拍子 事件 回呼 節拍 節奏 麥克風
records.d: 你來定義這個函式。麥克風（或鼓機）每聽到一個拍子，oav-p5 就呼叫它一次。
records.x: 用宣告 keyPressed() 的方式宣告它： 每個拍子呼叫一次，在拍子落下的當下，不是每個畫面一次。如果你比較想每個畫面自己問，改用 beat。 草圖只要定義了 beatDetected() 而沒有讀任何麥克風的值，第一次點擊或按鍵時就會啟動麥克風。鼓機開著的時候，鼓機的大鼓和小鼓也會呼叫同一個函式，而且不會為它去開麥克風。OAVp5.mic.on('beat', fn) 是不必定義全域函式的同樣功能，它會回傳一個停止監聽的函式。 你的函式如果出錯，草圖會繼續跑：錯誤會出現在 console，也會在 🎹 旁邊的卡片上顯示檔案和行號。 level 那一刻有多大聲，0..1（就是 micLevel 的值）。

records.k: kick snare hat drum callback event percussion 大鼓 小鼓 鈸 鼓 事件 回呼 打擊 麥克風
records.d: You define these; oav-p5 calls them when the microphone (or the drum machine) hears a kick, a snare or a hat.
records.x: The microphone splits what it hears into three drum-like bands and calls the matching function when each band jumps: 20–120 Hz for the kick, 150–800 Hz for the snare, 6–14 kHz for the hat. There is no machine learning in it, just a transient in a frequency band, so a bass voice can trigger a kick. When the drum machine plays, each of its hits calls the same functions: kick for the kick, snare for a snare, clap or rim, hat for a closed, open or pedal hat. A sketch written for the microphone therefore works with startDrums() unchanged. Defining one of them is not enough to open the microphone once the drum machine has started; reading micLevel (or calling startMic()) is. Without the drum machine, a sketch that defines any of them and reads nothing starts the microphone on the first click or key. level How strong the hit was, 0..1 (for the drum machine, its velocity).

records.k: kick snare hat drum callback event percussion 大鼓 小鼓 鈸 鼓 事件 回呼 打擊 麥克風
records.d: 你來定義這幾個函式。麥克風（或鼓機）聽到大鼓、小鼓或鈸的時候，oav-p5 會呼叫 kickDetected(level)、snareDetected(level)、hatDetected(level)。
records.x: 麥克風把聽到的聲音分成三個像鼓的頻段，哪個頻段突然跳高，就呼叫對應的函式：大鼓是 20–120 Hz，小鼓是 150–800 Hz，鈸是 6–14 kHz。裡面沒有機器學習，只是某個頻段出現瞬間的衝擊，所以低沉的人聲也可能觸發大鼓。 鼓機在播的時候，它的每一下也會呼叫同樣的函式：大鼓呼叫 kick，小鼓、拍手或 rim 呼叫 snare，閉合、開放或腳踏的鈸呼叫 hat。所以為麥克風寫的草圖，不用改就能搭配 startDrums()。 鼓機啟動之後，只定義其中一個函式並不會去開麥克風。要讀 micLevel（或呼叫 startMic()）才會。沒有鼓機的時候，草圖只要定義了其中任何一個、又沒有讀任何值，第一次點擊或按鍵時會啟動麥克風。 level 這一下有多強，0..1（鼓機的話就是力道）。

records.k: microphone mic on status permission allowed 麥克風 開著 狀態 權限 允許
records.d: Whether the microphone is running right now.
records.x: Use it to show a hint until sound arrives: if (!micIsOn) text("Allow the microphone", 20, 30);. Reading it never starts the microphone (unlike micLevel), so it is safe to check anywhere. The reason behind a false is in OAVp5.mic.state (off, asking, on, denied or unavailable) and, when something failed, OAVp5.mic.error. True once the browser has said yes and sound is coming in; false while the microphone is off, still asking, blocked or missing.

records.k: microphone mic on status permission allowed 麥克風 開著 狀態 權限 允許
records.d: 麥克風現在有沒有在運作。
records.x: 可以用它在聲音進來之前顯示提示：if (!micIsOn) text("請允許麥克風", 20, 30);。讀它不會啟動麥克風（跟 micLevel 不一樣），所以在哪裡檢查都安全。false 的原因看 OAVp5.mic.state（off、asking、on、denied 或 unavailable），失敗的時候還有 OAVp5.mic.error。 瀏覽器答應了、聲音進來之後是 true。麥克風關著、還在詢問、被擋下或不存在的時候是 false。

records.k: microphone mic volume loudness audio sound level input level vu meter decibel 麥克風 音量 聲音大小 聲音 收音 音量表 分貝
records.d: How loud the microphone hears things, from 0 (a quiet room) to 1 (shouting).
records.x: Read it in draw() the way you read mouseX: circle(width / 2, height / 2, 50 + micLevel 300) grows when someone talks. It is a loudness in decibels, which is how an ear hears it, measured from the room itself: the bottom of the scale follows the room's own noise (it settles within a second or two and rises at most 1.5 dB a second, so a voice never becomes the new silence), and −10 dBFS, shouting into a laptop, is 1. In practice a quiet room reads 0, a quiet voice about 0.4 to 0.6, shouting close to 1. If the microphone is quiet or far away, raise it with micSensitivity(). It follows the browser's animation frames rather than draw(), so a sketch running at frameRate(10) still reads the latest value, and the number stops changing while the tab is hidden (browsers pause animation frames there). Nothing to call. The first time a sketch reads micLevel (or bass, mid, treble, beat), oav-p5 asks the browser for the microphone, and every value stays 0 until you allow it. The page needs https or localhost. If the browser kept audio quiet until a click, the first click or key starts it. ?oav_mic=click makes only the 🎤 button and startMic() turn it on; ?oav_mic=off means nothing can. In the 🎹 panel the 🎤 button turns the microphone on and off by hand and shows the level. When the browser blocked it, a card beside the 🎹 says why and what to press: click the lock left of the address, set Microphone to Allow, then click the canvas. On openprocessing.org the sketch frame allows the…

records.k: microphone mic volume loudness audio sound level input level vu meter decibel 麥克風 音量 聲音大小 聲音 收音 音量表 分貝
records.d: 麥克風聽到的聲音有多大聲，從 0（安靜的房間）到 1（大喊）。
records.x: 像讀 mouseX 一樣在 draw() 裡直接讀：circle(width / 2, height / 2, 50 + micLevel 300)，有人說話圓就變大。它是以分貝量的音量，跟耳朵聽起來的感覺一致，而且是從房間本身量起：量表的底部跟著房間的底噪走（一兩秒內安頓下來，每秒最多往上爬 1.5 dB，所以人聲不會變成新的安靜），−10 dBFS（對著筆電大喊）就是 1。 實際上，安靜的房間是 0，小聲說話約 0.4 到 0.6，大喊接近 1。麥克風很小聲或離得很遠的話，用 micSensitivity() 把它調大。 它跟著瀏覽器的動畫畫面更新，不是跟著 draw()，所以用 frameRate(10) 跑的草圖讀到的還是最新的值。分頁被藏起來時數字會停住（瀏覽器在那時會暫停動畫畫面）。 不用呼叫任何東西。草圖第一次讀 micLevel（或 bass、mid、treble、beat）的時候，oav-p5 就會向瀏覽器要麥克風，在你按下允許之前所有的值都是 0。網頁要在 https 或 localhost 底下。如果瀏覽器在你點一下之前不讓聲音出來，第一次點擊或按鍵就會把它啟動。?oav_mic=click 表示只有 🎤 按鈕和 startMic() 能開。?oav_mic=off 表示什麼都開不了。 🎹 面板裡的 🎤 按鈕可以手動開關麥克風，並顯示音量。瀏覽器擋下麥克風的時候，🎹 旁邊會跳出一張卡片說明原因和怎麼處理：點網址列左邊的鎖頭，把麥克風設成允許，再點一下畫布。 在 openprocessing.org 上，草圖的框允許麥克風和 MIDI（2026-10-19 實際檢查過：它的 allow 清單有 microphone 和 midi），而且在那裡第一次讀 micLevel 就會去要麥克風。從 OpenProcessing 複製出來的嵌入碼沒有這個設定：要在那個 加上 allow="microphone"。 它背後的原始數字是 OAVp5.mic.rms（0..1）、OAVp5.mic.db 和 OAVp5.mic.floor（房間本身的底噪，單位 dBFS）。 麥克風開著的時候，每個畫面更新一次。麥克風關著、還在詢問、被擋下或根本沒有的時候，一直是 0。

records.k: sensitivity gain boost quiet microphone volume threshold 靈敏度 增益 放大 麥克風很小聲 音量
records.d: Makes the microphone more or less sensitive: micSensitivity(2) is twice as sensitive, micSensitivity() says what it is now.
records.x: The number multiplies what the microphone hears. On micLevel, 2 adds 6 dB; on bass, mid and treble it multiplies by 2 (they stay held to 1). Use it for a quiet microphone or a far-away voice: micSensitivity(3) in setup() adds about 9.5 dB. OAVp5.mic.gain is the same knob under the name oav-p5 0.3.0 used. v The new sensitivity, greater than 0 (kept between 0.05 and 20). Leave it out, or pass something that is not greater than 0, to change nothing. The sensitivity now in effect (1 until you change it).

records.k: sensitivity gain boost quiet microphone volume threshold 靈敏度 增益 放大 麥克風很小聲 音量
records.d: 調整麥克風的靈敏度：micSensitivity(2) 是兩倍靈敏，micSensitivity() 會告訴你現在是多少。
records.x: 這個數字乘在麥克風聽到的東西上。對 micLevel 來說，2 等於加 6 dB。對 bass、mid、treble 是乘以 2（最多還是 1）。麥克風很小聲或人離得很遠的時候用它：在 setup() 寫 micSensitivity(3) 大約加 9.5 dB。 OAVp5.mic.gain 是同一個旋鈕，用的是 oav-p5 0.3.0 的舊名字。 v 新的靈敏度，要大於 0（會被限制在 0.05 到 20 之間）。不傳，或傳不大於 0 的值，就什麼都不改。 現在生效的靈敏度（沒改過就是 1）。

records.k: microphone start enable permission getUserMedia promise 麥克風 開啟 啟動 權限 允許
records.d: Turns the microphone on and returns a promise that says whether it worked.
records.x: You rarely need it: reading micLevel and its friends already starts the microphone. Call it when you want to choose the moment (a button, the end of an intro) or know the answer: startMic().then((ok) => { … }). Calling it again while it is on, or while the browser is still asking, returns the same result. Browsers want a click before audio plays: call it from mousePressed() or a button handler if setup() is too early. It works whatever the mic option is, except ?oav_mic=off, where nothing can start the microphone. After stopMic(), only startMic() (or 🎤) turns it back on; reading micLevel does not. Resolves to true once the microphone is on, false if it was blocked, is missing, or the mic option is off.

records.k: microphone start enable permission getUserMedia promise 麥克風 開啟 啟動 權限 允許
records.d: 開啟麥克風，並回傳一個 promise，告訴你有沒有成功。
records.x: 通常用不到：只要讀 micLevel 之類的名稱，麥克風就會自己啟動。想自己決定時機（一個按鈕、片頭結束的時候）或想知道結果時才呼叫：startMic().then((ok) => { … })。已經開著、或瀏覽器還在詢問的時候再呼叫，會回傳同一個結果。 瀏覽器要先有一次點擊才讓聲音出來：如果在 setup() 裡太早，就放在 mousePressed() 或按鈕的處理函式裡呼叫。不管載入選項 mic 是什麼都能用，只有 ?oav_mic=off 例外，那時什麼都開不了麥克風。 呼叫過 stopMic() 之後，只有 startMic()（或 🎤）能再把它打開。讀 micLevel 不會。 麥克風開起來之後 resolve 成 true。被擋下、不存在、或載入選項 mic 是 off 的時候 resolve 成 false。

records.k: microphone stop disable mute off 麥克風 關閉 停止 靜音
records.d: Turns the microphone off and sets every microphone value back to 0.
records.x: It stops the microphone's tracks and closes its audio context, so the browser's "recording" indicator goes away. micLevel, bass, mid, treble and the rest read 0 again, and micIsOn is false. After stopMic(), reading micLevel does not turn the microphone back on: that needs startMic() or the 🎤 button. Resolves to false, the new state of the microphone.

records.k: microphone stop disable mute off 麥克風 關閉 停止 靜音
records.d: 關掉麥克風，所有麥克風的值都歸零。
records.x: 它會停掉麥克風的音軌並關掉它的音訊環境，所以瀏覽器上「正在錄音」的指示會消失。micLevel、bass、mid、treble 等等都回到 0，micIsOn 變成 false。 stopMic() 之後，讀 micLevel 不會再把麥克風打開：要用 startMic() 或 🎤 按鈕。 resolve 成 false，也就是麥克風的新狀態。

open-audiovisual (OAV) is a JavaScript framework for live audiovisual performance that runs in the browser. It is plain ES modules: no build step, no dependencies, no account. You clone the repository, run one file, and open a page. It handles the part every show rebuilds from scratch: MIDI plumbing, turning inputs into parameters, a timeline with scenes, a director's console, a performance mode for the performer, and a backstage page for the stage manager. You write the world, the piece itself. The pitch, a live instrument and the twenty-six example works are on the homepage.

Performers play the examples with a MIDI keyboard, a microphone, a camera, a phone, or the on-screen piano, and drive a show from the console. Coders write a world in about twenty lines and get inputs, mapping, timeline, console, sound and backstage from one createShow() call. AI agents read AGENTS.md, connect to the bundled MCP server, and write worlds inside a chassis that already works. See For AI agents.
textCopy Each layer has one job and a written contract (Architecture), so any layer can be replaced without touching the others. Two rules keep it that way; they are explained in Core concepts.

The core was extracted from The Last Input (Che-Yu Wu, 2026), a performance for piano and a living digital world at the IRCAM residency × C-LAB Taiwan Sound Lab in Taipei, played on a 49.4-channel speaker dome. The timeline, the chord semantics, many-to-many MIDI learn and OSC batching all ran a real fourteen-scene show before they were generalized here. The rule since then: the framework only grows features that a real show asked for. The mapping layer's ideas descend from libmapper's research on signal namespaces. The sister project WebToe is a node-based dataflow engine that imports TouchDesigner projects; WebToe is the engine, open-audiovisual is the show.

New here: Quick start, then Core concepts, then Writing a world. Building a show: Inputs, Mapping, Show control, Phones, relay & surfaces. Looking something up: Signals reference and Package reference. Something is wrong: Troubleshooting. Everything here is checked against the source in packages/. When this page and the code disagree, the code is right and this page is a bug: please open an issue.

Pick the one that matches what you already have. They get bigger as you go down. One line in a p5.js sketch. Any p5.js sketch (OpenProcessing, the p5 editor, your own page) can be played from a MIDI controller, from a controller drawn on screen, or from a phone, by adding one line at the top. Read p5.js in one line, and play the sketch that carries it: example 15. The same line also plays sound, runs a drum machine you can write as one line of rhythm, listens to the microphone and records a video; each has a ready-made sketch among the examples (16 to 26). One controller in a page. <oav-controller profile="akai-lpd8"> puts a controller you can play into any web page. Read MIDI controllers & embedding, and pick yours in the controller library. A whole show. A World plus one createShow() call assembles inputs, mapping, timeline, console, sound and backstage. Start from example 01 and keep reading below.

You need Node.js (any current version; CI runs the tests on Node 22) and a browser. There is nothing to install: no npm install, no bundler. bashCopy serve.js is a static file server with caching turned off (stale code on stage is a nightmare) that also hosts the phone relay at ws://<host>:8080/relay. Pass a port to use another one: node serve.js 3000. The same commands exist as npm scripts: commandwhat it runs npm startnode serve.js npm run monitornode packages/monitor/server.js, the backstage monitor on port 7457 npm run bridgenode packages/osc/bridges/osc-bridge.js, the OSC → UDP bridge on port 7456 npm testnode --test tests/*.test.js Open http://localhost:8080/examples/01-hello-particles/. Every example runs without hardware.

Not sure what your device can do? Open the device check. It looks at your browser, Web MIDI, microphone, camera and graphics, and says what to do about each. Nothing runs until you press a button, and nothing leaves your device. Web MIDI is the one that differs most between browsers (sources checked 2026-10-15): Chrome and Edge have it. Use them for a show. Since Chrome 124 any use of MIDI asks for permission, where before only system-exclusive access did (Chrome blog). Firefox has Web MIDI on desktop from version 108, after you install Firefox's site-permission add-on (Firefox 108 release notes). Safari on Mac, iPhone and iPad has no Web MIDI (caniuse). WebKit lists it as not implemented because of fingerprinting concerns (WebKit), and bug 107250 is still open and unassigned. Chrome on an iPhone or iPad is WebKit underneath, so it has none either. On a Mac there is a third-party Safari extension, Safari-WebMIDI; we have not tested it. Where the browser has no Web MIDI, there are three routes: Play on screen. Every controller in the library plays with a finger, and every event still fires. Use a phone as the controller. See Phones, relay & surfaces. A browser app for the iPad. MIDIWeb Browser is a third-party app for iOS 17.6 and later that gives pages Web MIDI. We have not tested it with open-audiovisual. On Windows 11 the built-in Windows MIDI Services (released 2026-02-17) give apps shared MIDI ports and a loopback, so loopMIDI is no longer needed to send MIDI from the browser to a DAW (Windows blog); see Play your DAW with it. Two more rules apply to every browser: Camera and microphone only work in a secure context: http://localhost or https://. Open the show on the machine that runs serve.js through localhost, not through its LAN address. Phones can join over plain http:// on the local network for touch, keys and the control surface. iOS only gives motion sensors and the camera to https:// pages (see Phones, relay & surfaces).

An example page has two parts: the stage on the left (the world renders there) and the side panel on the right. From the top, the side panel holds: The piano, with two checkboxes: keyboard turns on QWERTY playing, simulate performance starts a hands-free player. Transport: play/pause, previous/next scene, reset, the clock, the current scene, and a scrubber with one block per scene. Layers: what every layer is doing right now (events per second per input, active routes, world and FPS, what is leaving the browser). L1 · Input: MIDI devices (untick to mute one) and buttons for sources that need a click: 🎤 mic, 🖐 hands, 🕺 body. L2 · Mapping: every route, with a mute box and ✕ to remove it. L3 · Params: a slider per param, ✕ to clear an override, learn to map. L4 · Output — sound, when the show has sound: enable sound. Signals: a live meter for every signal. Each panel title collapses its panel. keyaction Spaceplay / pause the timeline ← →previous / next scene Rstop and rewind the timeline to 0:00 Tperformance mode (teleprompter) Ffullscreen Mshow/hide the on-screen MIDI controller (only in shows that set modules.midi.controllers)

On-screen piano: click or touch the keys; drag across them for a glissando. QWERTY: tick keyboard first (capture is off by default so letters do not steal the console's hotkeys). The keys A W S E D F T G Y H U J K O L P ; play 17 notes a semitone apart, starting at the piano's base note; Z/X shift an octave; hold Shift for a louder note. Simulate performance: a hands-free player noodles in a pentatonic scale with steps, leaps, triads and rests, so you can watch the mapping breathe. Drum machine (examples 03 and 06): a step sequencer whose signals have the same shape as the microphone's drum detection. On-screen MIDI controller (example 09): a picture of a known controller you can play with the mouse (the supported devices are listed on the controllers page); plug the real one in and the picture moves with your hands. All of these publish the same signals as real hardware, so nothing downstream can tell the difference.

A world is an object with params and four lifecycle functions. Hand it to createShow() and the rest of the show is assembled around it: jsCopy Play a note: the circle jumps and decays. Drag the size slider, or click learn next to it and turn a knob. That is the whole model: params for continuous control, signals for events.

Copy examples/01-hello-particles/ to examples/<nn>-<name>/ (the next free number). Its index.html already has an import map for every @openav/* package; the ?v= suffixes are cache stamps written by tools/stamp-version.mjs before a deploy. Write your world in main.js (Writing a world). Change the <title> in index.html. Add CDN script tags there if you use p5 or another renderer. Open http://localhost:8080/examples/<nn>-<name>/. An AI agent can do steps 1–2 with the MCP tool scaffold_world (For AI agents).

npm test passes (it covers the pure logic: chords, timeline, mapping, relay, surfaces, MIDI parsing and profiles, the site pages). The page loads with no console errors. One message is expected: if the backstage monitor is not running, the browser reports that ws://localhost:7457 refused the connection. The page retries quietly with a growing delay (up to 30 s). Run npm run monitor to make it go away. Press Space: the timeline plays and something changes over time. Tick keyboard and press A: the world reacts without any hardware. window.openav in the devtools console is the whole show (signals, params, mapper, timeline…), for poking at it by hand.
Six words carry the whole framework: signal, param, route, world, timeline, show. This chapter defines each one and the two rules that hold them together.

A signal is a named value that says what is happening: a knob's position, the loudness of the room, the height of a wrist, the consonance of the last chord. Every input package publishes signals into one registry (Signals from @openav/core) and does nothing else. Signals are the only currency of input. There are two kinds: kindholdsexampleread it with continuousa current value, usually 0..1midi/cc/74 = 0.42signals.get(name), signals.norm(name) pulsethe payload of the last eventmidi/note/on → { note: 60, vel: 0.8, … }signals.on(name, cb) Names are paths, source first: midi/cc/74, audio/band/low, pose/hand/right/y, phone/ab12/tilt/x, surface/main/hue. Ranges are normalized where that makes performance sense, and y axes are flipped so that 1 means raised, never raw pixels. A signal is declared with its range so that meters and learn can scale it: jsCopy set() on a name nobody declared defines it on the spot as continuous 0..1. If your values live elsewhere (degrees, MIDI note numbers), declare the range first. A knob, a raised hand and a chord's consonance are equal citizens in this registry. That equality is what lets you mix them: a hand can do whatever a knob does.

A param is a value the world listens to: hue, bloom, gravity. The world declares its params; each one is a line of schema: jsCopy Every frame each param resolves to one number: textCopy An override is sticky. Once a hand or a route has touched bloom, the timeline stops moving it until the override is cleared (✕ in the console, or params.clearOverride('bloom')). That matches the stage: when a human grabs a control, the score yields. The full field list is in Writing a world.

A route connects one signal to one param. Routes are plain data: jsCopy The mapper (@openav/mapping) holds the routes and applies them: it reads the signal, clamps it into a window (inMin..inMax), optionally inverts it, bends it with a curve, scales it into the param's range and, if asked, smooths it over time. One signal may drive several params and one param may listen to several signals. Learn binds the next signal that moves, which works for a knob and for a waving hand alike. Routes serialize to JSON, so a wiring is a file you can carry to the next venue. Details: Mapping.

A world is the piece: an object with a name, its params, and init / update / render / dispose. It reads resolved params every frame and may subscribe to signals for discrete events. It brings its own renderer: 2D canvas, p5, three.js, a WebToe patch, DOM, anything. The framework has no opinion. Details: Writing a world.

The timeline (@openav/timeline) is the score: keyframed automation per param, plus a list of scenes with titles and notes for the performer. It owns time; worlds never read the clock. Scenes may start before zero for a pre-show standby. Details: Show control.

A show is a world plus one createShow() call (@openav/show). It builds the signals registry, the params, the stage, the timeline, the mapper, the inputs you ask for, sound, the console, the backstage feed and the frame loop, and returns all of them. Every example is a world plus this call, so when the framework grows a module, every show can have it by declaring it. jsCopy

Two rules make the framework composable. They come in two forms: one says how the system is designed, the other says what that asks of anyone writing code for it. 1. Signals are the only currency of input. So: continuous control goes through params; discrete events may use signals. A world that reads signals.get('midi/cc/74') inside update() still works, today, with your controller. But it can no longer be driven by the timeline, by a dancer's wrist, by a phone, or by someone else's controller. You have welded the performance to one input. Declare a param instead and let a route connect midi/cc/74 → yourParam. The same world then works for everyone, and the console, the phone surface and learn all see the param. Events are different. "A note was struck", "a chord resolved", "a kick hit" are moments, not levels. Subscribing to them in init() is correct and encouraged; it is what makes a world react rather than just drift. 2. Worlds never know who is performing them. So: the shell never knows the work. A world reads params, and whether a value came from the timeline, a MIDI knob, a dancer or a slider is invisible to it. The same holds for the framework: never edit packages/* to make one example look right. A framework change has to make every work better. Switching works means swapping a world and its data; the shell stays.

open-audiovisual is a data-layer framework. Its entire value is that four layers and two spines stay cleanly separated, so any of them can be replaced without touching the others. This page states each layer's contract precisely.

One Loop (@openav/core) drives everything. This is the order createShow() runs each frame (packages/show/index.js): jsCopy Signals arrive between frames, whenever a device or a socket fires. An unsmoothed route writes its param immediately; a smoothed route sets a target that mapper.update(dt) glides toward. OSC output is not part of createShow(); if you use it, flush it from onFrame (Show control). dt is in seconds and clamped to 0.1 (new Loop(fn, { maxDt })), so a stall never makes a world explode. When the browser freezes requestAnimationFrame (the projection window went to the background), a Web Worker heartbeat keeps the loop ticking, about every 66 ms (~15 frames per second): the timeline, mapped signals and the backstage feed must not stop because someone switched windows. Param resolution order (the heart of the design): textCopy An override is sticky: once a knob touched bloom, the timeline no longer moves it until the override is cleared (✕ in the console). This matches performance reality — when a human grabs a control, the score yields.

Contract: input packages publish named, normalized signals into a Signals registry, and do nothing else. They never touch params or worlds. names are path-like: midi/cc/74, chord/consonance, pose/hand/right/y continuous signals declare {min, max} and always hold a current value pulse signals (kind: 'pulse') fire events; their payload is the event object anyone can subscribe: signals.on(name, cb) or signals.onAny(cb) Adding a new input modality (breath sensor, gamepad, stock ticker, weather API) means writing one class that calls signals.set() / signals.pulse(). Nothing downstream changes. That is the whole point. The inputs today: @openav/midi (hardware and on-screen controllers), keys, drums, audio (microphone), pose (camera body and hands), leap (Leap Motion / Ultraleap hands) and phones through remote and surface. Hardware a browser cannot open itself reaches it through a small local bridge that speaks a web protocol (leap runs one on ws://127.0.0.1:6437); the browser side is still one class that publishes signals. Analyzers sit between raw sources and mapping: @openav/chord subscribes to midi/note/on|off and publishes chord/*. It is still an input as far as the mapper is concerned; it just listens to other signals instead of a device.

Contract: the only component that connects signals to params. Routes are data: jsCopy many-to-many: one signal may drive several params; one param may listen to several signals (last writer wins). Learn adds, it never replaces. learn is generalized MIDI-learn: mapper.learn('bloom') binds the next signal that moves ≥5% of its range — a knob and a waving hand both qualify. routes serialize to JSON → mapping profiles are shareable files. Full reference: Mapping.

Contract: a World is { name, params, init, update(dt, state, io), render, dispose }. It reads state (resolved param values). It may subscribe to signals for discrete events (a note-on spawning a particle is an event, not a parameter), but continuous control must flow through params — otherwise your world stops being performable by the timeline or by other inputs. The Stage owns lifecycle and param aggregation and deliberately does not own a renderer. p5, three.js, 2D canvas, SVG, DOM — the framework has no opinion. Constitutional rule (inherited from The Last Input): the shell never knows the work. Switching works = swapping World + automation data. The shell stays. Full reference: Writing a world.

records.n: L4 · Output — two branches, video and audio, both optional
records.x: The output layer splits in two. Both branches hang off the same signals → mapping → params spine — sound is performable state, not a side effect. Video branch screen is the default output; performance mode (T) gives the performer a teleprompter while the audience sees the stage window fullscreen (F). recording (@openav/record): the work and the performer's camera composited into one canvas of an exact size (vertical 1080×1920 up to 4K) and recorded with the work's own sound by one MediaRecorder, so picture and sound share a clock. MIDI takes record the playing itself and replay it into the show. future: NDI gateway (see roadmap; groundwork lives in sister project WebToe). Audio branch MIDI out (external synths/DAWs): midi.send()/noteOn()/cc() — one throat, observable (onSend) so meters can watch everything, with a real panic(). In-browser synthesis: @openav/sound — a small pluggable engine contract (params, enable, noteOn, noteOff, set, dispose) with a Tone.js engine first (CDN, loaded only on enable) that plays instruments from a registry: a sampled grand piano, mallets, strings, organ, synth presets, one file per sound, picked from the console. Engine params register as sound/* — a knob, a hand, or the timeline plays the filter cutoff exactly the way it plays the visuals. The drum kit in @openav/drums is a second engine behind the same contract (pure WebAudio, no samples needed). OSC: browser → HTTP → osc-bridge.js → UDP (Spat, Reaper, TD, lights). Batched per frame; only the latest message per address survives a frame.

Pure logic, no DOM: params + automation keyframes + scenes → state(t). Scenes may start at negative t (pre-show standby). onSceneChange is the cue hook — fire sound, lights, prompts from it. A scene with hold: true stops playback at its end until the operator releases it. A show with structure adds the score to this spine (@openav/score): the show written as segment lengths, from which Score computes every start, end, cue and countdown, and Director runs the module that performs each segment (enter once, exit once, a crash switches off only that module). The timeline takes its scenes and total from the score, and the director plugs into it as a param layer: textCopy The score only decides when. What happens still reaches the world as params. Full reference: Score & Director.

The performance page streams JSON snapshots (throttled, ~15 Hz) over WebSocket to a dependency-free relay (server.js, hand-rolled RFC 6455). Any phone or laptop on the LAN opens the backstage page and sees: clock, scene, world, FPS, overrides, every signal and param, and a "stage feed lost" alarm. The monitor is a first-class citizen because a show without a backstage is a rehearsal.

records.n: Around the spines: console and phones
records.x: Console (@openav/console): the director's desk in the side panel, laid out by layer (Layers → L1 → L2 → L3 → L4 → Signals), plus performance mode. It reads the same objects the loop runs; it owns nothing. Phones (@openav/relay, @openav/surface, @openav/remote): phones and iPads join a room on a WebSocket relay and publish phone/* and surface/* signals. To the mapper they are one more input. See Phones, relay & surfaces.
A world is the only part of the framework you have to write. Everything else is assembly.

memberwhen it runswhat it gets name—a unique string; the stage registers worlds by name paramsread once, when the world is registeredan array of param declarations (below) init(ctx)when the world becomes active{ container, signals, params }. May be async; createShow() waits for it before the loop starts update(dt, state, io)every framedt in seconds (≤ 0.1), state = { key: value } for every param, io = { signals, … } render()every frame, right after updatenothing; draw from what update stored dispose()when another world is activatedrelease GPU objects, DOM, subscriptions surfaceoptionala phone control-surface layout; modules.remote uses it instead of generating one (Phones) container is an absolutely positioned layer that fills the stage. The stage empties it before every init, so you never clean up DOM someone else left. An exception thrown in update or render is caught and logged ([stage] update: / [stage] render:); the show keeps running.

fieldmeaning keythe name routes, automation and the console use. Required. labelwhat the console shows. Defaults to key. min, maxthe range. Overrides are clamped into it; routes scale into it. defthe value when there is no automation and no override. The core reads only def; autoSurface() alone also understands default. stepsnap overrides to multiples of step; on the timeline a stepped param holds each keyframe instead of interpolating. pulsetrue makes it a trigger instead of a level: the console shows a fire button, a mapped pulse signal (or a continuous signal crossing 0.5 upward) fires it, and the world listens with params.onPulse(key, cb). A pulse param has no value in state. groupa label for grouping. Engine params use 'sound'; autoSurface() makes one phone page per group. optionsnames for the values of a stepped param (['Circle', 'Petal', 'Star']); the phone surface shows them as a radio. surfacea hint for the phone surface: { type, color, label }. If two registered worlds declare the same key, they share one param (the first declaration wins).

Continuous control goes through params. Events may use signals. If your world reads signals.get('midi/cc/74') directly in update(), it still works — today, with your controller. But it can no longer be driven by the timeline, by a dancer, or by someone else's controller profile. You've welded the performance to one input. Route it: declare a param, let the mapper connect midi/cc/74 → yourParam, and the same world works for everyone. Events are different: "a note was struck", "a chord resolved", "an onset hit" are moments, not levels. Subscribing to those in init() is correct and encouraged — that's what makes worlds reactive rather than just modulated. Useful event signals: midi/note/on and midi/note/off (any keyboard, the on-screen piano, the simulated performer, a phone), chord/event (one analysis per played gesture), audio/onset, audio/kick, drum/kick. The full list is in the Signals reference.

The timeline is configured next to the world, in the createShow() call: jsCopy Keyframes are [seconds, value], sorted by time. Before the first keyframe the value is the first value; after the last, the last value. Scenes are sorted by t. title and note are what the performer reads in performance mode (T); the next scene and a countdown show under them. A scene with a negative t is a pre-show standby: with t: -30 the clock starts at -0:30. Try performing your world with only the timeline. If it is boring, a param is missing. More in Show control.
The stage does not own a renderer. Build one in init, destroy it in dispose.

createCanvas(container, { alpha = false }) from @openav/stage returns { canvas, ctx, fit, dispose }. fit() keeps the canvas the size of its container (device pixel ratio capped at 2) and returns { w, h } in CSS pixels; call it at the top of render(). Examples 01, 02, 03, 07, 08 and 09 use it.

Load p5 with a script tag in the example's index.html, then run it in instance mode inside the container. p5 draws on its own loop, so update only stores the state and render stays empty (examples 05 and 06): htmlCopy jsCopy

No bundled example uses three.js yet; this is the pattern. Add three to the example's import map ("three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js"), keep the renderer on this, and dispose everything: jsCopy

webtoeWorld() from @openav/world-webtoe turns a WebToe node patch into a world. The patch runs in an iframe; every frame in which a param changed, the resolved params are posted into it, and any patch parameter written as ext('name', fallback) listens (example 04): jsCopy Options: name (default 'webtoe'), app (default https://webtoe.openaudiovisual.com/), project, params, extra.
Anything you append to container is fine. The stage only calls your functions.
jsCopy All worlds' params are registered up front, so the console and the timeline can address any of them. stage.activate(name) does nothing if that world is already active.

update(dt, state, io) receives io. With createShow(), io holds only signals; add output handles once the show exists, and every world sees them: jsCopy Then, inside the world: jsCopy Often it is simpler to do it at the assembly level instead, as example 05 does: show.signals.on('midi/note/on', ({ note, vel }) => show.midi?.noteOn(note, Math.round(vel * 127), 1)). For instruments inside the page (a grand piano, mallets, strings, organ, synth presets), use modules.sound (Show control).

every continuous control is a param (try performing your world with ONLY the timeline) dispose() releases GPU objects and event subscriptions (worlds get switched live) world survives dt spikes (the Loop clamps to 100ms, but don't assume 16ms) nothing in the world reads the clock directly — the timeline owns time the page loads with zero console errors, and works with only the on-screen piano

Every input does one thing: publish signals. With createShow() you switch inputs on in modules; each one is also a plain class you can use on its own. The exact names and ranges are in the Signals reference. inputpackagemodules keydefaultpublishes MIDI hardware@openav/midimidion (false turns it off)midi/… on-screen MIDI controllers@openav/midimidi: { controllers }offmidi/<device>/<control> on-screen piano, QWERTY, simulated performer@openav/keyskeyson (false removes it)midi/note/on, midi/note/off drum machine@openav/drumsdrumsoffdrum/…, midi/note/on on channel 10 microphone@openav/audioaudiooffaudio/… chord analysis@openav/chordchordoffchord/… body (camera)@openav/poseposeoffpose/… hands (camera)@openav/posehandsoffhand/… hands (Leap Motion)@openav/leapleapoffleap/… phones and iPads@openav/remoteremoteoffphone/…, surface/…, midi/note/… Sources that need permission or a user gesture (microphone, camera) are created by createShow() but only start when you click their button in the console's L1 · Input panel: 🎤 mic, 🖐 hands, 🕺 body.

createShow() creates a Midi engine and calls enable() on startup, so the browser may ask for MIDI permission when the page opens. Devices can be plugged in and out during the show; the L1 · Input panel lists them, and unticking one mutes it without unplugging it. Every incoming message publishes two families of names: legacy (what most worlds use, any channel): midi/note/on and midi/note/off pulses, midi/cc/<n> (0..1), midi/bend (−1..1); per channel: midi/ch/<ch>/cc/<n>, midi/ch/<ch>/note/<n> (velocity 0..1 while held, 0 on release), midi/ch/<ch>/bend, midi/ch/<ch>/pressure, midi/ch/<ch>/poly/<n>. A note-on payload is { note, vel, velocity, ch, device }: vel is 0..1, velocity is the raw 1..127, ch is 1..16, device is the port's slug. With two or more devices connected, each also publishes under its own slug so their controls do not collide: midi/<slug>/cc/<n>, midi/<slug>/note/on, midi/<slug>/note/off, midi/<slug>/bend. The slug comes from the port name (Arturia MiniLab 3 → arturia-minilab-3; a second identical unit gets -2), so a device that drops out and comes back keeps its routes. The legacy names keep publishing too, so a route on midi/cc/74 hears every device. Clock messages are ignored. Program change, transport and SysEx are not published (SysEx access is never requested). Using it without createShow(): jsCopy filterOut is a case-insensitive regular expression on input port names that are ignored. The default, 'IAC', keeps the macOS IAC bus out, because a show that sends MIDI out through IAC would otherwise hear itself. See Troubleshooting if you want to receive from IAC. MIDI output is described in Show control.

modules: { midi: { controllers: { profile: '<profile id>' } } } adds an on-screen picture of a known controller. Plug that controller in and the picture switches to it and moves with your hands; without one, play the picture with a mouse or a finger. Its controls publish midi/<device>/<control> names, and controllerRoutes() writes the routes that connect them to params. The MIDI controllers & embedding chapter covers profiles, learning unknown devices, LED feedback and embedding; the supported devices are on the controllers page.

records.n: On-screen piano, QWERTY and the simulated performer
records.x: @openav/keys is on by default. It mounts a piano above the console with two checkboxes, keyboard (QWERTY capture) and simulate performance. Options (modules.keys): base (lowest note, default 48), octaves (default 2), sim (show the simulate checkbox, default true), capture (show the keyboard checkbox, default true). It publishes midi/note/on { note, vel, ch: 0 } and midi/note/off { note, ch: 0 }. Note the differences from hardware: ch is 0 and there is no velocity or device field. A world that only reads note and vel works with both. QWERTY (after ticking keyboard): A W S E D F T G Y H U J K O L P ; play 17 notes a semitone apart, starting at base; Z/X move an octave (base stays between 24 and 84); Shift adds 20 to the velocity. While capture is on, the piano claims every letter key (preventDefault); Space, arrows and digits pass through to the console. The simulated performer (SimPlayer) plays a pentatonic scale an octave above base: mostly steps, sometimes leaps and triads, real rests. From code: show.keys.sim.toggle(true). jsCopy

modules: { drums: true } adds a 16-step, four-lane sequencer (kick, snare, hat, clap) with patterns (four on floor, breakbeat, half time, latin, sparse), a tempo slider (60–180 BPM, default 112), swing and humanized timing. Tick drum machine to start it. It plays its own synthesized kit (no samples) and publishes: drum/kick, drum/snare, drum/hat, drum/clap: pulses { level }; drum/<lane>/env: a 0..1 envelope per lane that decays in about 0.12 s, ready to map straight onto a param; midi/note/on { note, vel, ch: 10 } with General MIDI notes (kick 36, snare 38, clap 39, closed hat 42). The shapes match what the microphone's drum detection publishes (audio/kick, audio/kick/env…), so a world mapped to a kick cannot tell a real bass drum from the machine. Example 06 routes both to the same params. Options (modules.drums): engine (another sound engine), autoEnableEngine (default true: the kit's audio engine is switched on by the first hit, no extra click).

modules: { audio: true } creates an AudioAnalyzer; the microphone starts when you click 🎤 mic. (Example 06 writes audio: 'mic'; any truthy value works.) Echo cancellation, noise suppression and auto gain are turned off so the analysis hears the room as it is. Published every frame: audio/rms (smoothed loudness), audio/peak, audio/band/low (20–250 Hz), audio/band/mid (250 Hz–2 kHz), audio/band/high (2–8 kHz), audio/centroid (brightness), and the pulse audio/onset { rms } with a 100 ms refractory time. Drum detection splits transients by band: audio/kick (20–120 Hz), audio/snare (150–800 Hz), audio/hat (6–14 kHz), each a pulse { level } with a matching …/env envelope. Tip Real-world levels rarely reach 1. Speech often sits around 0.05–0.2 RMS and band energies are averages across many FFT bins. Narrow the route's window, for example { source: 'audio/rms', target: 'energy', inMax: 0.3 }. jsCopy

modules: { chord: true } (or { chord: { window: 80 } }) adds a ChordDetector and feeds it every midi/note/on and midi/note/off. It groups notes struck within window milliseconds (default 80) into one gesture and publishes, per gesture: chord/consonance (−1..1), chord/count (number of notes), chord/root (lowest MIDI note); chord/event, a pulse carrying the whole analysis: fieldmeaning notes, count, root, vel, pcssorted notes, how many, the lowest, mean velocity (0..1), pitch classes consonancemean of pairwise interval weights, −1..1 (a single note is 1) isConsonant, isDissonanttwo or more notes and consonance > 0.25 / < −0.15 isTriadthe chord type is major, minor, sus2, sus4, dim or aug thirdsFractionshare of adjacent gaps that are 3 or 4 semitones ("genuinely stacked thirds") dissonanceLevel0 none · 1 mild (a storm warning) · 2 severe (a true cluster) chordTypesingle, major, minor, sus2, sus4, dim, aug, maj7, min7, dom7, halfdim7, maj9, min9, dom9, six, min6, cluster, or chord This is not a music-theory library; it is a performance-semantics layer built for a piece where consonance makes a garden flourish and clusters make it decay (example 02). detector.analyze(notes, vels) is a pure function you can call yourself.

modules: { pose: true } adds a PoseTracker (one body), modules: { hands: true } a HandTracker (two hands, 21 points each). The camera starts when you click 🕺 body or 🖐 hands. Both use MediaPipe Tasks Vision (0.10.14), loaded from jsDelivr with its model from Google's storage the first time you enable it; the inference runs on your machine and no video leaves it. The view is mirrored by default (mirror: true), like a mirror on stage, and y is flipped so 1 means raised. Body: pose/present, pose/hand/left/x|y, pose/hand/right/x|y (wrists), pose/hand/left/v, pose/hand/right/v (wrist speed), pose/hands/spread, pose/height (nose height: crouch ↔ stand), pose/lean (−1..1). Hands: per side, hand/<side>/present, hand/<side>/x|y (palm), hand/<side>/pinch/index and hand/<side>/pinch/middle (thumb tip to finger tip), hand/<side>/spread (index tip to pinky tip). Distances are divided by palm size, so moving toward the camera does not change a pinch. A closed pinch reads near 0: use invert: true on the route when closing should raise the value (example 03). Both trackers draw their skeleton on a 2D context: tracker.skeleton(ctx, w, h).

modules: { leap: true } adds a LeapInput. Browsers cannot read the sensor, so one small bridge per machine does: node packages/leap/bridge/leap-bridge.mjs (needs Ultraleap Hand Tracking installed; --mock gives two animated hands without a sensor; bash packages/leap/bridge/install.sh keeps it running at login on macOS). It serves ws://127.0.0.1:6437 on loopback only. The console's L1 · Input panel shows which link is missing (bridge, tracking service, device) and draws the hands; its simulate button turns the mouse into hands. Signals: per side, leap/hand/<side>/present, x|y|z (palm in the interaction box, 0..1, y up, z toward you), pinch, grab, roll|pitch|yaw (radians), speed, fingertips leap/hand/<side>/<finger>/x|y|z; leap/hands, leap/both/distance, leap/status; pulses pinch-start|pinch-end, grab-start|grab-end per side and leap/both/pinch-start|pinch-end, with hysteresis (a pinch starts above 0.86 and ends below 0.5). Joints for drawing the hand are on leap.hands. The same bridge answers old leap.js sketches on /v6.json, and serves raw hand lines on /raw (example 12, package README).

modules: { remote: true } lets phones join the show over the relay that serve.js hosts. Their sensors publish phone/<id>/… (tilt, acceleration, rotation, knocks, touch, light), mirrored to phone/any/…; the control surface publishes surface/<page>/<widget>; the phone's piano publishes midi/note/on|off like a keyboard. The show page itself can read its own motion sensors on a phone with localSensors(). Everything is in Phones, relay & surfaces.

An input is anything that calls signals.set() or signals.pulse(). Here is the pointer as an instrument: jsCopy Name it source first (breath/pressure, weather/wind), declare its range, and everything downstream (meters, learn, routes, the phone surface) works without changes.
The mapping layer is where "what happened" becomes "what it means". The Mapper (@openav/mapping) is the only component that connects signals to params, and everything it knows is a list of routes.

A route is a plain object. Only source and target are required; addRoute() fills in the rest: fielddefaultmeaning source—signal name, e.g. midi/cc/74, hand/right/pinch/index, phone/any/tilt/x target—param key, e.g. bloom, sound/cutoff inMin, inMax0, 1the window of the signal that is used; values outside it are clamped outMin, outMaxthe param's min, maxthe range written into the param curve'linear'linear, exp, log or smooth invertfalseflip the normalized value (1 − x) before the curve smooth0glide time in seconds (0 = instant) enabled(absent = on)false mutes the route idassigneda number, used to remove the route jsCopy In createShow(), the same objects go in routes: [...].

When a signal arrives, every enabled route whose source matches runs these steps, in order: Window: x = (value − inMin) / (inMax − inMin), clamped to 0..1. Invert: if invert, x = 1 − x. Curve: x = curve(x). Scale: out = outMin + (outMax − outMin) · x. Write: with smooth: 0, the param is overridden with out (and clamped and snapped to its step). With smooth > 0, out becomes a target that mapper.update(dt) glides toward every frame.

curveformulafeel linearxas the hand moves expx²slow start, fast end: fine control near the bottom log√xfast start, slow end: fine control near the top smoothx²(3 − 2x)gentle at both ends (smoothstep) An unknown curve name falls back to linear.

inMin/inMax say which part of the signal matters; outMin/outMax say where it lands. Typical uses: a bipolar signal: { source: 'midi/bend', inMin: -1, inMax: 1 }, or a phone tilt { source: 'phone/any/tilt/x', inMin: -1, inMax: 1 }; a quiet signal: { source: 'audio/rms', inMax: 0.3 } uses the whole param range for the levels a voice actually reaches; a knob that only sweeps part of a param: { source: 'midi/cc/1', target: 'hue', outMin: 180, outMax: 270 }; an inverted relation without invert: outMin: 1, outMax: 0. Warning outMin/outMax default to the target param's range at the moment the route is added. If the param does not exist yet, they default to 0..1. In createShow(), routes are added before the sound engine registers its sound/* params, so a declared route to sound/cutoff needs explicit outMin: 100, outMax: 8000.

smooth is a time constant in seconds: after smooth seconds the param has covered about 63% of the distance to the new value (a one-pole filter, k = 1 − e^(−dt/smooth) per frame). 0.05–0.15 hides the steps of a MIDI knob or a 30 Hz phone stream; 0.2–0.5 makes a hand feel heavy. The glide starts from the param's current value, so the first movement never jumps.

When the target is a pulse param, the route fires it instead of writing a value: a pulse source (midi/note/on, audio/kick, drum/kick, phone/any/knock…) fires it on every event; a continuous source fires it when the normalized value crosses 0.5 upward (a phone-surface button going from 0 to 1, a fader pushed past the middle). curve, invert, smooth and the output range do not apply to pulse targets.

One signal may drive many params (add several routes with the same source), and one param may listen to many signals. When two routes write the same param, the last one to write wins. Learn adds a route; it never replaces one. The patch bay design plans per-route combine (last, max, add, avg) and label fields; they are not implemented yet.

A route writes its param as an override, and overrides are sticky: as soon as a mapped signal moves, the timeline stops driving that param. Clearing the override (✕ next to the param, or show.params.clearOverride(key)) hands it back to the timeline until the signal moves again. A smoothed route keeps writing its last target every frame once its signal has arrived, so its param stays overridden even after ✕ and even when the route is muted. Remove the route (✕ in L2 · Mapping) to give the param back to the timeline for good.

Click learn next to a param in L3 · Params (or call mapper.learn('bloom')), then move something. The mapper binds the first signal that: moves by at least 5% of its declared range from where it was when learn started (a knob, a fader, a hand, a phone tilt), or fires, if it is a pulse (a key, a pad, a knock). The new route has the defaults: linear, no smoothing, the param's full range. Edit it afterwards if it needs a curve. Clicking learn again cancels. Learn adds: a param that already has a route keeps it and gets a second one. To bind a whole list, the L2 · Mapping panel has 🎛 map knobs in order: it arms learn for the first param, you turn one knob, it is bound and the next param is armed. skip, back, stop (or Esc) steer it. In code it is LearnWizard (details). Caution Any pulse binds immediately. Untick simulate performance and stop the drum machine before you learn, or the next note they play becomes the route. When one MIDI message publishes several names (midi/cc/74, midi/ch/1/cc/74, and with two devices midi/<slug>/cc/74), learn binds the first one, midi/cc/74, which hears every device. Change the source to the per-device name if you need one device only.
The L2 · Mapping panel lists every route as source → target with a checkbox (mute) and ✕ (remove). In code: jsCopy

The mapper saves its routes to localStorage under openav.map.<profile>. createShow() uses the world's name as the profile (or the profile option) and: loads the saved routes if there are any, otherwise adds the declared routes; when a saved profile exists, still adds every declared route whose source → target pair is missing, so new routes in code arrive; saves every 3 seconds. So learned routes and edits survive a reload. The flip side: if you change the curve or smoothing of a declared route in code, the saved copy of that source → target pair wins. To start clean, pass profile: false (routes come from code on every load, as in example 09) or remove the saved profile: jsCopy To carry a wiring to another machine or another world, use a map file (next section).

records.n: Map files: export, import and share
records.x: The L2 · Mapping panel has three buttons under map knobs in order: ⬇ export downloads the routes as oav-map-<world>.json. ⬆ import picks a map file. You can also drop a .json anywhere on the page. Import replaces the routes; the new set is remembered at once. clear removes every route (click twice). On the next load the world's declared routes come back, as on a first visit. Below the buttons the panel says what the last import did: how many routes came in, and every route it skipped and why. A file that cannot be read says so and changes nothing.

jsonCopy Routes are named by signal and param, never by id, so a file travels between worlds: a route whose param this world does not have is skipped and listed; a route whose signal nothing in this show can produce (say leap/palm/x without a Leap Motion module) is skipped and listed. Signals that only appear when the first message arrives (midi/…, surface/…, phone/…, osc/…, key…, take/…) are kept and counted as waiting; when the file's world is a different one, the range.out is dropped so each param keeps its own range (the in window, curve, smoothing and invert come along); version newer than this build reads is refused with a message. A bare array from mapper.toJSON() (the old way) still imports, as version 0. Files over 256 KB or with over 500 routes are refused.

textCopy ?map=<url> fetches the file when the page opens and loads it like an import. It accepts a same-origin address (relative paths included) or an absolute https one; http: to another host, data:, javascript:, file: and addresses with a login are refused. A cross-site file must be served with CORS (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *; raw GitHub and gists do this). The show starts regardless: if the address is refused, the fetch fails or the file is bad, the panel shows the reason and the routes stay as they were. An explicit ?map= beats the remembered wiring, and what it loads is remembered like any import. In code, createShow({ map: 'maps/a.json' }) does the same and map: false ignores ?map=.

The mapper saves its routes to localStorage (openav.map.<world>) every 3 seconds and right after an import or clear, one slot per world name, so the next visit starts where you stopped. Every read and write is wrapped: in a private window or with storage blocked nothing breaks, the wiring just is not remembered. In code: jsCopy

Several packages generate routes in this same shape: autoSurface(world.params) (@openav/surface) builds a phone control panel and the surface/<page>/<widget> → param routes for it, with smooth: 0.04; routesFromLayout(layout, params) does the same for a hand-written layout (Phones, relay & surfaces). controllerRoutes(profile, { knob1: 'hue', pad1: 'burst' }) (@openav/midi) writes routes from an on-screen controller's controls (MIDI controllers & embedding).
jsCopy onChange() runs when routes change (for UIs); onLearn(route, signalName) runs when learn binds.
The parts that turn a sketch into a performance: the one-call assembly, the timeline, the console, performance mode, the backstage monitor, and the ways sound and data leave the browser.

parts you did not ask for are null. The same object is window.openav, for the devtools console. The frame order is…
